# Isaiah Chapter 58 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 157r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ISA_058_page_001.jpg

---

**58:6** "Is-not this the-fast [tsom] I-choose [evchareihu]: to-loose [patteach] the-bonds [chartsubbat] of-wickedness [resha], to-undo [hatter] the-straps [aguddot] of-the-yoke [motah], and-to-send [shalach] the-oppressed [retsutsim] free [chofshim], and-every yoke [motah] you-break [tenatteiqu]?"

**58:7** "Is-it-not to-share [paros] your-bread [lachmekha] with-the-hungry [la-ra'ev], and-the-afflicted [aiyyim] homeless [merudim] you-bring [tavi] [to your] house [bayit]; when you-see [ki-tir'eh] the-naked [arom] you-cover-him [vekhissito], and-from-your-own-flesh [mi-besarkha] you-do-not hide [lo tit'allam]?"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.6-7 — True fasting:** Isaiah's most direct social justice passage. Real fasting is not abstaining from food — it is freeing the oppressed, sharing bread with the hungry, sheltering the homeless, clothing the naked. Religion without justice is empty ritual.

*— EMET*
